skill.name: service-mesh-observability
skill.description: Implement observability for service meshes with metrics, tracing, dashboards, alerts, and service topology guidance for Istio and Linkerd.
skill.summary: Plan service mesh telemetry, tracing, dashboards, and alerts for Istio and Linkerd environments.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown code fences, and the URL findings are documentation or in-cluster references, so those are false positives. The OpenTelemetry examples include all-interface listeners, anonymous Kiali access, and insecure TLS settings that require production hardening.

remediation.issue: OpenTelemetry collector listeners bind to all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Limit collector exposure with Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, service scope, authentication, and explicit production guidance before users copy the manifest.

remediation.issue: Kiali example uses anonymous authentication across all namespaces.
remediation.suggestion: Default to token or OpenID authentication and scope accessible namespaces to the smallest required set.

remediation.issue: Jaeger exporter example disables TLS verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use verified TLS or mTLS for production exporters, or label insecure TLS as development-only guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Anonymous Kiali Access Across Namespaces
semantic_findings.description: The Kiali example uses anonymous authentication and makes all namespaces accessible. Copying this into a shared cluster can expose service topology and traffic metadata without login controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited Kiali manifest explicitly sets anonymous auth and wildcard namespace access. The risk depends on deployment exposure, but the insecure default is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure TLS Setting in Telemetry Exporter
semantic_findings.description: The OpenTelemetry example sets tls.insecure to true for the Jaeger exporter. This disables transport verification in copied deployments unless limited to a trusted test network.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Jaeger exporter configuration directly includes tls.insecure: true. The example may target a lab cluster, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Service mesh telemetry is hard to connect across metrics, traces, dashboards, and alerts. This skill provides practical templates for Istio, Linkerd, OpenTelemetry, Kiali, Prometheus, and Grafana.
actual_capabilities: Provides Istio Prometheus and ServiceMonitor templates for mesh metrics collection.
Includes PromQL queries for request rate, error rate, latency, TCP connections, and request size.
Shows Jaeger tracing configuration with sampling guidance for service mesh traffic.
Lists Linkerd viz commands for dashboards, routes, live taps, and service edges.
Provides Kiali, OpenTelemetry Collector, Grafana dashboard, and Prometheus alert examples.
Defines alerting rules for high errors, high latency, and certificate expiration.
limitations: It provides templates and guidance, not automated cluster deployment or validation.
It assumes Kubernetes and an existing Istio or Linkerd service mesh.
Sample manifests require production hardening before use in shared clusters.
It does not size storage, retention, or cost controls for a specific environment.

use_cases.title: Build Mesh Dashboards
use_cases.description: Create Prometheus and Grafana coverage for traffic, errors, latency, and topology.

use_cases.title: Investigate Service Latency
use_cases.description: Use metrics, traces, and Linkerd viz commands to isolate slow service paths.

use_cases.title: Define Mesh SLO Alerts
use_cases.description: Turn golden signals into alert rules for error budgets and certificate health.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Mesh Observability Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an existing mesh
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the service-mesh-observability skill to create a starter observability plan for an Istio mesh. Include metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alerts.

prompt_templates.title: Create Istio Metrics Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the service-mesh-observability skill to design PromQL queries for Istio request rate, 5xx errors, P99 latency, and service dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Linkerd Service Latency
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the service-mesh-observability skill to build a Linkerd troubleshooting workflow for high latency between a frontend service and backend service.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Production Telemetry
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the service-mesh-observability skill to review production telemetry settings for sampling, authentication, namespace scope, TLS, and alert quality.

output_examples.input: Plan observability for a new Istio mesh.
output_examples.output: A structured rollout covering Prometheus scraping, Grafana panels, Jaeger tracing, Kiali topology, and alert rules for golden signals.

output_examples.input: Investigate high latency for one service path.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting sequence using P99 latency metrics, service dependency views, trace sampling, and route-level traffic inspection.
A configuration checklist covering receivers, exporters, batching, sampling, TLS settings, and network exposure controls.

best_practices: Adjust tracing sample rates for production traffic and data retention goals.
Protect dashboards and collectors with authentication, network policy, and namespace scoping.
Validate PromQL queries against real traffic before using them for alerts.
anti_patterns: Using anonymous dashboard access in shared clusters.
Copying development sampling rates into production.
Adding high-cardinality labels to every metric.

faq.question: Which meshes does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Istio and Linkerd, with supporting examples for Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, OpenTelemetry, and Kiali.

faq.question: Can it deploy observability tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and command examples that users must review, adapt, and apply in their own environment.

faq.question: Does it include production alert examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes alert concepts for error rate, latency, and certificate expiration, but thresholds need local tuning.

faq.question: Can it help with distributed tracing?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Jaeger and OpenTelemetry patterns, including sampling and trace collection for service traffic.

faq.question: Does it replace vendor documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes common patterns and links to upstream resources for detailed product behavior.

faq.question: What should teams review before production use?
faq.answer: Teams should review authentication, namespace scope, TLS settings, sampling rates, retention, and network exposure.
